lessons.title: Discipline Is the Soul
lessons.imageAlt: Charles Willson Peale — George Washington in the uniform of a colonel of the Virginia Regiment (1772), full portrait painting, public domain
lessons.source: George Washington, Instructions to Company Captains, Fort Loudoun, 29 July 1757 (Founders Online)
lessons.quote: Permit me, before I finish ... to recommend, and I do in the strongest manner I can to you and your Officers; to devote some part of your leisure hours to the study of your profession, a knowledge in which can not be attained without application ... Discipline is the soul of an army. It makes small numbers formidable; procures success to the weak, and esteem to all.
lessons.lesson: Washington was 25 and in charge of a small, green regiment. He did not ask his captains for more men or better gear. He asked them to use their free hours to study their job. Skill does not come by itself. It comes from steady work when no one makes you do it. That daily habit is the discipline he means. It lets a few people do the work of many, and it earns respect that talk never will.
